Run a validation plan

Source: R/validation-run.R
run_validation.Rd

Usage

run_validation(
  plan,
  dir,
  previous = NULL,
  refit = c("on_change", "never", "always"),
  workers = NULL,
  ...,
  .fitter = NULL
)

Arguments

plan

A bmmtools_validation_plan.

dir

The directory every stage caches under, created if missing.

previous

NULL, or an earlier result to compare with: a bmmtools_validation, its result.rds, or the directory it was run in. The comparison is the result's changes.

refit

"on_change" (the default) reruns a stage when its inputs differ from those of its stored result, or when it has none; "never" reads what is stored and marks every stage without a stored result "skipped"; "always" reruns every stage, with refit = "always" for the prior fits of prior_check() and sbc(). The recovery grid keeps its cells by their cache keys in every case (see recovery_grid()); delete <dir>/recovery/cells to refit them.

workers

Reserved for parallel recovery cells (#19). Only NULL, which runs the cells one after another, is accepted.

...

Passed to the fitter of every stage, after the plan's sampler lists, so an argument given here wins (backend, iter, refresh, ...). The arguments sbc() refuses in its ..., such as cores, do not reach the calibration. A prior, or an abbreviation of it such as pri, is refused, here and in the plan's sampler lists: the calibration's prior is the plan's sbc$prior, and the recovery stage fits under bmm's default priors.

.fitter

The fitting function of every stage, bmm::bmm() by default. Tests inject a stand-in so that nothing is compiled.

Value

A bmmtools_validation: a list with plan; run_info, the run_info() rows written when the run started and ended, with when and the elapsed seconds; stages, a tibble with one row per stage (stage, order, title, required, status, issue, reason, started, finished, seconds, resumed, message, warnings); one element per stage holding its result object as the stage function returned it, or NULL; numbers, the card_numbers() tibble; verdicts, the verdict_table(); headline, a list with state ("validated", "not validated", "not judged" or "incomplete"), stages (the stages the state names) and text; and changes, the compare_validations() of previous and this run, or NULL. The same object is written to <dir>/result.rds.

Details

Executes a validation_plan() stage by stage into dir, where every stage keeps its result and its status. A rerun reads the stages whose inputs have not changed and runs the rest, so an interrupted run is resumed by calling it again.

Stages

status is "ok"; "failed", with the condition message in message; "skipped", when a stage it reads produced nothing or refit = "never" found nothing stored; "stale", when refit = "never" read a result made from other inputs or software versions than this plan's (the result is kept, but it is not this plan's); or the plan's own status for a stage that does not run ("not built", "not applicable", "excluded"). A failed stage is never an error of run_validation().

The headline is "incomplete" while a required stage that exists is not "ok"; "not validated" when a required criterion failed; "not judged" when none failed but one could not be evaluated (a response without a known range, say); and "validated", printed with the plan version and hash, only when every required criterion was evaluated and met.

What each stage runs:

  • run_record: run_info(), written to <dir>/run-info.rds before any other stage and again, with the end row, after the last.

  • prior_predictive: prior_check() on data simulated at the plan's prior-check design point, under bmm's default priors and, when the calibration has its own, under that one too.

  • sbc: sbc() at the plan's design point under the plan's prior.

  • recovery: recovery_grid() over the plan's grid at the population, SD and subject levels, with the model correlations where there are at least two subject-varying parameters, every cell gated by check_convergence() and contracted against a prior-only fit (prior_sd = "fit").

  • computation, identifiability, individual_differences: tables read off the recovery grid's cells and summary.

  • data_requirements: the read-off, smallest_design() of the subject-level r_low along n_trials at the plan's read_off_n_subjects, at read_off_r_low and at 0.70 and 0.90; one row per subject-varying parameter and threshold with n_subjects, term, threshold, smallest and status. It has no coverage condition of its own (see verdict_table()).

  • agreement: cross_check() of the fit of the largest design's first replication against the plan's reference.

Resuming

A stage's inputs are the plan fields it reads, its seed, the ... of the call, the fitter, the versions of bmm, brms, bmmtools, the Stan toolchain (and SBC for the calibration) and, for a stage read off the grid, the grid's inputs. They are hashed into the stage's status file, and a stage is read rather than rerun while its hash is unchanged and its status is "ok", so a new bmm release reruns every stage. A grid with failed cells is rerun, which retries those cells and reads the others from their cache, and a stage read off the grid is computed again whenever the grid was not read. The whole plan is written to <dir>/plan.rds; a plan whose hash differs from the stored one is announced and replaces it.

See also

validation_plan(), card_numbers(), verdict_table(), compare_validations().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
plan <- validation_plan("ezdm", seed = 20261024)
result <- run_validation(plan, "validation/ezdm")
result
verdict_table(result)
} # }
